title: Alina Müller signs with PWHL Hamilton after being left unprotected by Boston Fleet: Source
content:
Swiss star forward Alina Müller has signed a three-year deal with the PWHL’s new expansion team in Hamilton, according to a source briefed on the situation.

The PWHL’s four new expansion teams — Detroit, Hamilton, Las Vegas and San Jose — currently have a three-day window, which began Friday, to acquire five players through signings and, if necessary, a player selection process.

PWHL expansion rules allowed the eight existing teams to protect three players from being poached by the league’s newest teams. Boston general manager Danielle Marmer opted to use her protections on defenders Haley Winn and Megan Keller, as well as goalie Aerin Frankel.

That left Müller, a 28-year-old star center and one of Boston’s top scorers, exposed to the league’s six-phase expansion roster-building process.

Müller was under contract with the Fleet until 2027-28, which meant she could not be forcibly signed by an expansion team via the “Expansion Franchise Offer” contract. However, according to the league’s rules, any player left unprotected is eligible to sign during Phase 2.

That Müller chose to leave Boston comes as a bit of a shock. She was Boston’s first draft pick (third overall) in the inaugural PWHL Draft and played her college career at Northeastern in the city. On Thursday, Marmer said in a media availability that she would do everything she could to keep Müller in Boston.

“It strictly came down to the strategy and the path that I felt was best to move forward in rebuilding this team,” Marmer said of the decision not to protect Müller. “I told her how much she means — I’m going to get emotional — how much she means to this organization and this city. I told her I love her, and that starting now it’s the path to get her back here in Boston.”

Müller, who won an Olympic bronze medal at the Milan Olympics, adds to what is shaping up to be a solid Hamilton core. General manager Meghan Duggan already made a splash on Friday, signing former Ottawa captain Brianne Jenner and former New York goalie Kayle Osborne to three-year standard player agreements.

“I could not be more excited to announce that my new chapter begins today with PWHL Hamilton,” Jenner said in an Instagram post on Friday. “As a family we have deep ties to the Golden Horseshoe, and I can’t wait to get started and help build the culture and identity of the team that gets to represent this region.”

Hamilton has until 1 p.m. ET Monday to sign two more foundational players. If the team fails to reach five signings, there will be a player selection process Monday evening. Only players identified on an expansion team’s 20-player “Exclusive Negotiation Target List” are eligible to be signed during Phase 2.

Existing teams can lose a maximum of three players who are under contract for the 2026-27 season during this phase. The PWHL’s full rules are here.
